events.summary:
The team has done strong work establishing the symptom shape (step at ~13:16-13:22Z, no recovery), the direction (outbound: pricing-engine is a victim waiting on market-data-service), the flat-load/flat-local-CPU exoneration of pricing-engine, and the complete absence of any code/config change in-window (count=1 unrelated auth deploy, count=0 config changes, partial=false). That correctly kills H3 (rejected, no topological path, 2h gap, wrong symptom signature) and H5 (rejected: no release, flat CPU, all errors outbound).

But the ranking of the live hypotheses is not yet grounded. H1 and H2 are distinguished only by DIRECTION of causality between the same two facts (the cache-miss storm at 13:22:25Z and market-data CPU ~90% at 13:22Z), and the critical hop of H1 — "redis-cache stopped serving quote keys / failed over / evicted / restarted" — is explicitly ASSUMED with zero cache-side telemetry retrieved. The observed cache-miss log line is emitted by market-data-service, i.e. it is a client-side report of a miss, not evidence from the cache; it does not by itself prove the cache failed rather than that market-data stopped writing/refreshing keys or its own process was stalled. F10's claim that market-data CPU saturation "precedes or is coincident with" pricing onset is within bucket-resolution ambiguity (13:22 4-min bucket vs a coarse 420s pricing bucket whose true onset is inferred as ~13:22), so temporal order does not decisively separate cause from effect here. The same single fact (cache misses) is asserted as "supporting" H1 and "contradicting" H2 — that dual use is a ranking artifact, not discrimination.

H4 is dead on the numbers (flat pricing request rate, no market-data volume evidence, only an UNVERIFIED precedent cited), so the real decision is H1 vs H2. The decisive evidence — redis-cache's own metrics/logs (uptime/restart, connected_replicas, evictions, keyspace hits/misses, memory, connections) and market-data's memory_pct/GC/restart counters — was never queried; the observability budget ran out before the cache component was examined. This is not redundant confirmation: a clean cache with a degraded hit ratio flips the ranking to H2, and a restart/failover/eviction spike confirms H1. It is obtainable (redis-cache is a first-class component with a dependency edge) and blocking for the top-hypothesis ranking. Confidence cap held below the stated 0.48.

events.objective: Decisive test between H1 (cache-side failure drives everything) and H2 (market-data-side problem makes the cache look cold). Pull redis-cache's OWN telemetry for 2026-04-09T13:00-14:00Z, reported per bucket vs a 12:30-13:15Z baseline: uptime/restart or failover/sync events, connected_replicas, keyspace hits vs misses, evictions, expired_keys, memory_used/maxmemory, connected_clients, CPU. Explicitly state whether a restart, node promotion, or empty-replica/full-resync occurred near 13:22Z. In the same task pull market-data-service memory_pct, GC pause time/count, and restart counters for 13:00-14:00Z: does CPU rise to ~90% with GC pause time spiking or a restart at 13:22Z (H2), or do memory/GC stay flat while CPU tracks cache-rebuild work (H1)? A failover/restart/eviction byte-spike or degraded hit ratio with healthy memory confirms H1; healthy cache with keys simply absent because market-data stopped writing, plus GC/restart at 13:22Z, flips to H2.

Bound the true blast radius and test the alternative that an external feed or sibling quote-path component is primary (making market-data's cache misses and CPU saturation its local effect). Check exchange-gateway and any other quote-path component (order-service, api-gateway, quote/BFF) for latency_p99, error_rate, and request_rate in 2026-04-09T13:00-14:00Z. Report whether exchange-gateway or any other quote-path service degraded at ~13:22Z alongside market-data-service, and whether any such degradation precedes market-data's CPU/miss onset.

events.statement: redis-cache hit_ratio_pct has a clean step change at the 13:22Z bucket: it was 95-97% for the entire 12:30-13:20Z baseline (e.g. avg 95.9 at 13:20Z, max 96.34) then dropped to avg 10.82 / max 11.2 at 13:22Z and never recovered above 25.37% by 14:00Z (slowly climbing 10.8 -> 25.4). This is a decisive collapse in cache serving at exactly the onset.

redis-cache memory_pct (memory_used/maxmemory proxy) ALSO collapses at the same 13:22Z bucket: from ~68-76% throughout 12:30-13:20Z (avg 71.36 at 13:20Z) to avg 6.1 / max 6.19 at 13:22Z, then slowly refilling (6.66 at 13:24Z, 16.48 at 14:00Z). An instantly emptied dataset that then refills from scratch is the signature of a flushed/restarted instance or an empty-replica full-resync, not of gradual key expiry or eviction.

redis-cache connected_clients drops sharply at the same 13:22Z bucket: baseline ~296-327 clients (avg 312.88 at 13:20Z) falls to avg 41.8 (max 43.2) at 13:22Z and 38.77 at 13:24Z, then returns to ~300-320 from 13:26Z onward. A near-total client disconnect/reattach followed by reconnection is consistent with the cache instance restarting/being failed over at 13:22Z.

redis-cache CPU stayed flat across the event: 20.45-24.37% over the whole 12:30-14:00Z window, with 21.91 avg/22.39 max at the 13:22Z bucket and no step. The cache did NOT enter a CPU/eviction-pressure regime; it went from serving ~96% hits to serving ~11% hits at unchanged CPU, which is a data-emptiness problem, not a cache resource-saturation problem.

market-data-service memory_pct stayed FLAT across the onset: 12:30-13:20Z ranged ~58.77-64.48 avg (max 67.13), and the 13:22Z onset bucket was avg 58.8 / max 60.74 with 62.01 at 13:24Z and no memory step through 14:00Z (window min 56.87, max 67.13, mean 61.96). So the market-data CPU saturation (F10, ~90%) is NOT accompanied by memory growth, arguing against a GC/allocator-blowup mechanism for H2; its CPU spike looks like work (rebuild loops), not memory pressure.

Combined reading: the redis-cache step at 13:22Z (hit_ratio 95.9%->10.82%, memory 71.4%->6.1%, clients 312.9->41.8, CPU unchanged) is an emptied dataset that refills slowly from 6% upward, i.e. a cold/empty cache instance — the exact signature of the HIST-107 'Cold cache storm after redis failover / empty replica promotion' precedent. The market-data cache-miss storm first log (F11, 13:22:25Z) and its CPU step (F10, 13:22Z bucket) follow this redis change by seconds, consistent with H1 (cache-side failure drives everything) rather than H2 (market-data compute primary), since market-data memory is flat and nothing was released/deployed (F2/F14).

events.answer: redis-cache's own telemetry shows a hard step change at the 13:22Z bucket exactly: hit_ratio collapses from ~95-96% to 10.82%, memory_used drops from ~71% to 6.1%, and connected_clients falls from ~300-330 to 41.8 (then 38.77) while redis CPU stays flat at ~22% and no eviction/memory-pressure signature appears. That is the fingerprint of an emptied/restarted primary with a fresh empty replica dataset (HIST-107 'cold cache storm after redis failover'), i.e. the cache stopped serving keys at 13:22Z — supporting H1 over H2. market-data-service memory_pct stayed flat (~58-66%) across the onset, so no memory-side/GC pressure is visible (its GC metric is not exposed at all), which argues against H2's compute/GC-saturation premise.

events.summary: H1 is adequately proven after round 2. The blocking gap I flagged in round 1 — no cache-side telemetry — is closed: redis-cache's own metrics show a hard step at the 13:22Z bucket with hit_ratio 95.9%→10.8%, memory 71.4%→6.1% then slow refill, connected_clients 312.9→41.8 with reattach, all at FLAT redis CPU (~22%) and with no eviction signature. That is a server-side data-emptiness event, not eviction or load, and it cannot be produced by an app-side client (market-data-service holds only a cache-client edge), which kills H2's premise. H2's sole causal hop is flagged evidence-free, and F30 (market-data memory flat ~58-66% across onset) contradicts its GC/memory mechanism. Temporal chain now rests on verified cache-side facts rather than log ordering: cache emptiness at 13:22Z → market-data cache-miss storm from 13:22:25Z (289 rebuilds 6.8-8.1s) → market-data CPU 46%→90% with flat memory → outbound deadline-exceeded (all 192 errors, first 13:23:57Z, up to 8456ms) → pricing-engine p99 60ms→2228ms with flat local CPU and flat traffic (~642 req/s) → api-gateway p99 step as victim. Blast radius is fully explained: redis-cache is the only shared=true node called by both pricing-engine and market-data, so both degrade; exchange-gateway (flat 120-144ms) and order-service (flat 140-166ms) are exonerated, killing the external-feed alternative; H3 (no topological path, 2h gap, wrong signature), H4 (flat traffic/CPU), and H5 (no release, flat CPU, all errors outbound) are rejected on verified contradictions. Residual uncertainty is only the sub-variant of the cache event (restart vs failover/empty-replica promotion vs FLUSH); redis-cache exposes no uptime/restart/keyspace/replica metrics (not_found, permanent), so this cannot be directly observed and asking again would repeat a failed source. The mechanism and mitigation (warm cache / fix replica sync, per HIST-107) are unchanged across sub-variants, so this is not worth further rounds during an outage. Confidence capped at 0.85 rather than the stated 0.72-to-0.9 range: confidence is higher than stated on the mechanism, but the unobserved trigger and within-bucket temporal ambiguity in the 13:16-13:22Z region keep a residual margin.

The team has done strong work establishing the symptom shape (step at ~13:16-13:22Z, no recovery), the direction (outbound: pricing-engine is a victim waiting on market-data-service), the flat-load/flat-local-CPU exoneration of pricing-engine, and the complete absence of any code/config change in-window (count=1 unrelated auth deploy, count=0 config changes, partial=false). That correctly kills H3 (rejected, no topological path, 2h gap, wrong symptom signature) and H5 (rejected: no release, flat CPU, all errors outbound).

But the ranking of the live hypotheses is not yet grounded. H1 and H2 are distinguished only by DIRECTION of causality between the same two facts (the cache-miss storm at 13:22:25Z and market-data CPU ~90% at 13:22Z), and the critical hop of H1 — "redis-cache stopped serving quote keys / failed over / evicted / restarted" — is explicitly ASSUMED with zero cache-side telemetry retrieved. The observed cache-miss log line is emitted by market-data-service, i.e. it is a client-side report of a miss, not evidence from the cache; it does not by itself prove the cache failed rather than that market-data stopped writing/refreshing keys or its own process was stalled. F10's claim that market-data CPU saturation "precedes or is coincident with" pricing onset is within bucket-resolution ambiguity (13:22 4-min bucket vs a coarse 420s pricing bucket whose true onset is inferred as ~13:22), so temporal order does not decisively separate cause from effect here. The same single fact (cache misses) is asserted as "supporting" H1 and "contradicting" H2 — that dual use is a ranking artifact, not discrimination.

H4 is dead on the numbers (flat pricing request rate, no market-data volume evidence, only an UNVERIFIED precedent cited), so the real decision is H1 vs H2. The decisive evidence — redis-cache's own metrics/logs (uptime/restart, connected_replicas, evictions, keyspace hits/misses, memory, connections) and market-data's memory_pct/GC/restart counters — was never queried; the observability budget ran out before the cache component was examined. This is not redundant confirmation: a clean cache with a degraded hit ratio flips the ranking to H2, and a restart/failover/eviction spike confirms H1. It is obtainable (redis-cache is a first-class component with a dependency edge) and blocking for the top-hypothesis ranking. Confidence cap held below the stated 0.48.

challenges.issue: The causal-chain head ('redis-cache stops serving quote keys — failover/empty-replica promotion/eviction/restart') is [ASSUMED] with no cache-side telemetry at all. The only 'cache failure' evidence (F11) is a WARN log emitted BY market-data-service, i.e. a client-side observation of a miss; it cannot distinguish cache-side failure from market-data-side write failure/expiry/stall. H1's top rank rests on an unverified hop.

Temporal order is not established between market-data CPU saturation and the cache misses to the precision needed. F10 concedes onset is 'precedes ... or is coincident', and F13 admits the pricing 13:16Z bucket is coarse (420s) with true onset inferred as ~13:22Z. A cause cannot be shown to precede its effect within the same 4-minute bucket.

H2 is listed as contradicting F11, yet F11 (cache misses) is equally consistent with H2's stated mechanism (a saturated service fails to refresh/read its cache, so entries expire). Using the same finding as support for H1 and contradiction of H2 does not discriminate the two; H2 is neither tested nor excluded. Its own head ('internal resource pressure / GC / unrecorded restart') is likewise [ASSUMED] because memory_pct, GC and restart metrics were never queried.

H4 cites F19, which is UNVERIFIED and describes HIST-113, a pricing-engine CPU-saturation incident the current telemetry contradicts (flat pricing CPU). No volume/market-activity metric was ever pulled. H4 is not so much tested as unsupported; it should be formally rejected on the flat request-rate evidence rather than left at 0.18 with an invalid citation.

Deployment inventory covers only 08:00-14:59Z and only via deploy/config APIs; a redis restart or failover (the H1 trigger) would never appear there, so the 'no change aligns with onset' conclusion is silent on the very class of event H1 posits. GAP acknowledged but not remediated.

critiques.summary: H1 is adequately proven after round 2. The blocking gap I flagged in round 1 — no cache-side telemetry — is closed: redis-cache's own metrics show a hard step at the 13:22Z bucket with hit_ratio 95.9%→10.8%, memory 71.4%→6.1% then slow refill, connected_clients 312.9→41.8 with reattach, all at FLAT redis CPU (~22%) and with no eviction signature. That is a server-side data-emptiness event, not eviction or load, and it cannot be produced by an app-side client (market-data-service holds only a cache-client edge), which kills H2's premise. H2's sole causal hop is flagged evidence-free, and F30 (market-data memory flat ~58-66% across onset) contradicts its GC/memory mechanism. Temporal chain now rests on verified cache-side facts rather than log ordering: cache emptiness at 13:22Z → market-data cache-miss storm from 13:22:25Z (289 rebuilds 6.8-8.1s) → market-data CPU 46%→90% with flat memory → outbound deadline-exceeded (all 192 errors, first 13:23:57Z, up to 8456ms) → pricing-engine p99 60ms→2228ms with flat local CPU and flat traffic (~642 req/s) → api-gateway p99 step as victim. Blast radius is fully explained: redis-cache is the only shared=true node called by both pricing-engine and market-data, so both degrade; exchange-gateway (flat 120-144ms) and order-service (flat 140-166ms) are exonerated, killing the external-feed alternative; H3 (no topological path, 2h gap, wrong signature), H4 (flat traffic/CPU), and H5 (no release, flat CPU, all errors outbound) are rejected on verified contradictions. Residual uncertainty is only the sub-variant of the cache event (restart vs failover/empty-replica promotion vs FLUSH); redis-cache exposes no uptime/restart/keyspace/replica metrics (not_found, permanent), so this cannot be directly observed and asking again would repeat a failed source. The mechanism and mitigation (warm cache / fix replica sync, per HIST-107) are unchanged across sub-variants, so this is not worth further rounds during an outage. Confidence capped at 0.85 rather than the stated 0.72-to-0.9 range: confidence is higher than stated on the mechanism, but the unobserved trigger and within-bucket temporal ambiguity in the 13:16-13:22Z region keep a residual margin.

challenges.issue: The triggering runtime event (restart vs failover/empty-replica promotion vs FLUSH) is inferred, not observed: redis-cache exposes no uptime/restart/keyspace/replica metrics. This does not change the mechanism, blast radius, or mitigation, so it is residual rather than blocking.

Temporal separation between redis-cache's 13:22Z step, market-data's step, and pricing-engine's onset remains within bucket-resolution ambiguity (coarse 420s pricing bucket, true onset inferred ~13:22Z). Direction is now pinned by the cache-side server-side signature rather than by log ordering, so this no longer threatens the ranking.

Its one causal hop (market-data internal resource pressure/restart at 13:22Z) is evidence-free; market-data restart counter was never read. F30 (flat memory) plus a server-side emptiness that a client cannot produce makes this very unlikely to be the driver, but the counter is technically unretrieved.
redis-cache evictions_per_min was never obtained (budget exhaustion). Memory collapse plus flat CPU already argues against an eviction storm, so this does not alter the mechanism.
